correctness.rationale: An independent spectral dual check uses the trace-one normalized projector Z_F on the first real Fourier plane (the plane's projector divided by two). Its quadratic edge strains are 1/n on spokes and c_n/n on rims. The trace-one projector Z_H onto the hub-versus-rim line has strains (n+1)/n and 0. A trace-one positive dual test on the constant-orthogonal subspace upper-bounds lambda_2 by tr(ZL). For t<c_n mix Z_F with coefficient (n+1)t/(c_n+nt) and Z_H with the remaining coefficient; strains are proportional to the prices and give the claimed value. For t>=c_n use Z_F alone, giving B/n and excluding positive rim weights when t>c_n. The uniform Laplacian has hub contrast eigenvalue (n+1)a and first rim eigenvalue a+c_n b, so the stated weights attain each bound. At equality the first harmonic lies in the bottom eigenspace of the constant-orthogonal restriction (the dual gives it positive weight in every regime). The imaginary part of its rim eigenvector equation forces equal rim weights because sin(2pi/n) is nonzero for n>=3. The real part then forces equal spokes. At equality of prices the remaining hub bound is precisely (n+1)a>=B/n. This covers the triangular rim and the full closed critical segment. The segment is an exposed optimal face of the lifted semidefinite problem, not a face of the weight-budget simplex itself.
residual_risks: This is for the combinatorial Laplacian and the stated linear cost only. The frozen script's finite trials are corroborative and were not used as proof of rigidity.
